subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests within one shared reviewer/run, and what exact input should define the cache key?
rationale: The redundant billing is real, but letting a later exec bypass a fresh model review changes approval-adjacent semantics and needs explicit owner intent before an automated repair.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance using the complete reviewed input or rendered prompt as the key, without persisting or creating durable approval state.

options.title: Memoize only low-risk allows
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, timeout, and error results uncached for a narrower behavior change.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept the repeated model cost to preserve one-model-review-per-exec semantics until stronger security or live billing evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance using the complete reviewed input or rendered prompt as the key, without persisting or creating durable approval state.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and related merged policy work make this the strongest available owner for the reviewer cache and approval-boundary decision.
